page: Amazon Web Services t3a.2xlarge is an x86_64 burstable general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, while AVX-512 extensions are absent. The configuration does not include local storage, relying on network-attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results reflect the limitations of the older Zen-architecture processor and the burstable credit model. In synthetic CPU tests, the t3a.2xlarge achieved a PassMark CPU score of 6,846.73 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2,630.0, placing raw computational throughput in the lower percentiles relative to modern dedicated cloud hardware. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 22.36 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 11.20 GB/sec for write operations. However, hardware-accelerated tasks such as PassMark encryption scored reasonably well at 6,395.92, and the instance demonstrated Redis write throughput of 4.97 million operations per second.

The t3a.2xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-centric deployments that experience variable or spiky CPU utilization. While the burstable CPU allocation and lack of dedicated local NVMe storage make it unsuitable for sustained compute-intensive tasks, continuous compilation pipelines, or large-scale machine learning inference, it provides balanced capacity for staging environments, development servers, moderate web applications, and asynchronous task workers.
description: Amazon Web Services t3a.2xlarge is an x86_64 burstable general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7571 architecture. Offering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores at 2.2 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it targets workloads requiring substantial memory without sustained peak CPU usage. It includes 2 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth, no local instance storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark scores place its raw processing throughput in lower percentiles compared to modern non-burstable platforms, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2,630.0. Cryptographic throughput remains competent due to native AES and SHA instruction support, achieving 6,395.92 on PassMark encryption. The t3a.2xlarge serves as a cost-conscious option for development setups, microservices, background processing, and low-concurrency web tiers requiring a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio.
